title: Public money per licensed child-care place
question: For each child-care operator with a State contract or City early-childhood money, how much public money is promised for every child the State licenses it to look after?
finding: Among 23 San Francisco operators holding State contracts or City early-childhood payments, the money for 2025-26 works out at a middle figure of $26,457 per licensed place. 3 come out at twice that or more, led by Wu Yee Children's Services at $144,539 a place ($77.3 million against 535 licensed places). 1 contract holder with $2.6 million listed for 2025-26 has no open licence in the State file: Companeros Del Barrio (closed Companeros Del Barrio, Inc. (44, 2024-12)).
how: Licensed places are the capacity of every open child-care centre licence the organization holds in the State licensing file of 8 November 2026 (family child-care homes excluded). Money is the largest State child-care and preschool contract figure published for State fiscal year 2025-26 under each programme, plus what the City Department of Early Childhood paid in City fiscal year 2026. Places in 2022 are rebuilt from the same State file, which carries the date each licence was first issued and the date it closed. City money is taken from the Controller's table of every payment, not from its narrower nonprofit-spending table, which keeps contracted services only. Left out of it, each picked out by the payment file's own label, are: loans; money the City collects for a benefit district and hands over (the district's own assessments); benefit-plan payments from a trust fund; and debt service. The fiscal year is the one printed on each payment, which can be later than the year the payment was made.
limits: A licence is a ceiling on children present at one time; it is not enrolment. State figures are contract maximums, not payments. Several of these organizations pass money on: resource-and-referral agencies pay vouchers to other providers, and some contracts cover children in partner family child-care homes that are not on the operator's own licence. An organization may hold licences under a name this match missed, which would overstate its figure or wrongly show it with no licence; the State's contract lists also carry last year's figure forward until a contract is formally ended. Citations and complaints are as the State lists them for open sites. The figure keeps grants and contracts the nonprofit-spending table lacks, emergency purchases, and aid paid through an organization (day care assistance, rent assistance paid on behalf of clients, in-home care contract payments). Part of that aid passes on to others, so it is a real City payment but not all of it is payment for the organization's own work. For the 444 organizations profiled, that leaves out $78.8 million of loans (9 organizations), $210.5 million of money the City collected for a benefit district and handed over (11 organizations) and $495.1 million of benefit-plan payments from a trust fund (1 organization), fiscal 2019 to 2026. District assessments are covered on the screen “Benefit districts: assessments in, City grants on top”, which keeps assessments and City grants apart.
